title: Patterson on I-5: Exit 434, the Paris-Plan Town
meta: Patterson, California sits at exit 434 on I-5. Learn about its Paris and Washington, D.C.-style street plan and the Apricot Capital title.
intro: Patterson is at exit 434 on Interstate 5, east of the freeway with the Diablo Range rising close on the west. Founder Thomas Patterson laid the town out like Washington, D.C., and Paris, with circles and streets spreading like spokes, and in 1971 its chamber of commerce named it the Apricot Capital of the World. I-5 Buddy's talking guide tells this story as you pass.

faq.q: What exit is Patterson on I-5?
faq.a: Patterson is at exit 434 on I-5 in California. The exit numbers count up from the Mexico border.

faq.q: Why is Patterson laid out like Paris?
faq.a: Thomas Patterson wanted his town to look different from other farm towns, so he planned it like Washington, D.C., and Paris, with circles and streets spreading out like spokes. Its main streets were planted with palms, eucalyptus and sycamores.

faq.q: Why is Patterson called the Apricot Capital of the World?
faq.a: In 1971 the Patterson chamber of commerce named the town the Apricot Capital of the World.

faq.q: Where is the nearest rest area to Patterson on I-5?
faq.a: Going north, Westley Rest Area is at mile 444.9, about 11.8 miles from Patterson, and it serves both directions. Going south, Dos Amigos Vista Point is at mile 390.0, about 43.1 miles away; the data does not say which direction it serves.
